Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone 18 series in September as usual this fall, but this year's product launch will echo in several ways the abnormal circumstances of the iPhone release during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.

How this fall's iPhone launch differs from Apple's usual practice

Apple has many extremely successful products, but the iPhone has always been its flagship, accounting for a large share of the company's overall revenue.

Precisely because of this, Apple naturally tends to maintain consistency in iPhone launches. By sticking to a predictable schedule for new iPhone releases, Wall Street and consumers can both feel more at ease.

Generally speaking, Apple unveils new iPhones in early September—usually four new models—and all of them go on sale later in the same month.

But 2020 saw abnormal circumstances due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

The 2020 fall iPhone lineup was not unveiled until October, and only two of the new models went on sale initially, with the remaining two delayed until November.

This year there are rumors that Apple's launch plans will see similar abnormalities.

Although the September launch event is expected to proceed as usual, Apple may not put all new iPhone models on sale at the same time.

As in 2020, only two models may be available for purchase initially: the iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

The much-anticipated foldable model, the iPhone Ultra, is expected to be unveiled in September, but rumors suggest its release date may be slightly delayed, potentially arriving several weeks after the Pro models go on sale.

Apple may also break with tradition in terms of the total number of new iPhone models.

If rumors that the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 will be pushed back to spring 2027 prove true, only three new models will debut this fall—making it the smallest fall iPhone lineup since 2019.

Whether for strategic reasons, challenges from the global memory crisis, or the difficulty of mass-producing an entirely new foldable device, Apple's fall 2026 in several respects may replay the situation of 2020.

What new surprises would you like to see Apple bring to this fall's iPhone launch? Let us know in the comments section.
